record_reviews.summary: Darwin restates Hancock’s three observations about Verruca/Clisia excavation, reports his own examination across species, then lays out a numbered argument against mechanical boring and toward hypothetical chemical action: no boring apparatus, basal membrane mechanics, larval cement, protective epidermis, and contrasting slate/marble/Laminaria supports. He asks Hancock to inspect specimens on soft non-calcareous materials, asks about Alcippe, Ibla and Scalpellum sexes, and requests return of a schoolboy Mollusca manuscript.
record_reviews.date_assessment: 25 December 1852 explicit; the text distinguishes Hancock’s prior three facts from Darwin’s fresh results and questions. Later Living Cirripedia citations in footnotes are publication aids, not evidence of knowledge before this letter.

record_reviews.summary: Thirteen-block Darwin memorandum-like letter gives a complete Alcippe summary: mouth and palpi, cirri and the homology of the cushion, absent rectum/anus, sensory organs, female and rudimentary male organs, metamorphosis, parasitic males with detailed morphology and counts, mechanical excavation and larval discs, and unresolved affinities. Darwin repeatedly marks uncertainty (“Eye not discovered,” “hardly examined,” “I cannot demonstrate,” “dreadfully puzzled”) while separating observations from analogies to Anelasma, Ibla, Alepas and Lithotrya. Inline diagrams occur in paragraphs 11 and 12 and were retained as visual evidence requirements.
